seat-balance-3p-4p.text: Under random play every 3p seat must win 0.28-0.38 and every 4p seat 0.20-0.30; rotate the start player every round and never give the first seat first pick or first bid without a compensating cost.

guaranteed-termination.text: Every game needs a hard terminator independent of player choices (deck exhaustion or round cap); random play must end within 300 turns at every player count, or s2_playable fails at max_turns=1500.

no-dominated-fallback-action.text: No legal action may be strictly dominated in expected value by another (e.g. 'stash for half value' vs 'bid'); give every fallback a situational upside such as immunity, multiplier, or later reuse.

cap-greedy-dominance.text: Greedy-vs-random win rate must be 0.55-0.75 at 2p and above 1/n+0.12 at 3p/4p; hit the ceiling with hidden info or counterplay, never with extra random draws.

hand-cards-need-competing-uses.text: When hand-management is a listed mechanic, each card must have at least two competing uses or a reason to hold it (reuse limit, end-game bonus for kept cards), not just 'play highest that clears the threshold'.

bluffing-needs-private-info.text: Any hidden-role, hidden-VP, bluffing or simultaneous-selection design must make the hidden part decisive: hidden points >= 30% of a typical winning score, or the hidden role gets an action no other role has.

game-length-cap.text: Estimated play time must stay under 25 min at every player count and total turns under 45; size the deck and hand so a game ends within that budget.

decision-density-floor.text: Mean legal actions per turn must exceed 5 and the share of forced (single-option) turns must stay under 0.05 at every player count.

draw-rate-cap.text: Draw rate must stay under 0.05 at every player count; define a full deterministic tiebreak chain (score, then a secondary resource, then seat furthest from start) so ties cannot remain.

rulesheet-worked-example.text: The rulesheet must contain one fully worked example turn and one worked end-of-game scoring example with concrete card values.

edits.reason: Both batch3 games flagged seat-order advantage: undercroft 3p 0.293/0.373/0.333, fence 3p 0.413/0.33/0.257 while 2p was even.

edits.text: Every game needs a hard terminator independent of player choices (deck exhaustion or round cap); random play must end within 300 turns at every player count, or s2_playable fails at max_turns=1500.
edits.reason: undercroft failed gauntlet s2_playable with 'exceeded max_turns=1500' at 2p and 3p and needed a rules.py fix.

edits.text: No legal action may be strictly dominated in expected value by another (e.g. 'stash for half value' vs 'bid'); give every fallback a situational upside such as immunity, multiplier, or later reuse.
edits.reason: fence: stash (floor half value) was judged strictly worse than bidding, so 8.6 mean legal actions still scored depth 6; padding options does not buy depth.

edits.text: Greedy-vs-random win rate at 2p should stay under 0.75; include at least one decision where the myopic value-maximizing play is wrong (delayed payoff, saving high cards, bluffing cost).
edits.reason: undercroft greedy 0.875 and fence greedy 0.783 / MCTS 1.0 at 2p; judge cited both as solvable by simple heuristics, depth 5-6.

edits.text: When hand-management is a listed mechanic, each card must have at least two competing uses or a reason to hold it (reuse limit, end-game bonus for kept cards), not just 'play highest that clears the threshold'.
edits.reason: undercroft: fight decision was 'weapon value + suit + die vs threshold', judged mechanical; hand-management contributed no tradeoff and depth scored 5.

edits.text: Betting-and-bluffing or simultaneous-selection designs must give each player private information beyond their own hand (hidden lot values, secret goals, a second concurrent lot) so bluffs are not solved by card counting.
edits.reason: fence: one shared lot with no private info beyond hand was judged to have limited bluffing depth once players count cards; fun 6.

edits.reason: 7 of 10 games had 2p greedy >= 0.88 (bindle 1.0, open-outcry 0.992, mutiny/watchfire 0.983); lamplighter failed the gauntlet at >=0.97 everywhere while watchfire (4p 0.28) and crossgrain (3p 0.39, 4p 0.24) failed the floor and needed fix passes.

edits.reason: Judges flagged length as too long for the depth in mutiny (32-50 min), crossgrain (32-64), bindle (28-29, ~69 turns), millwright (28) and watchfire (48 turns); every game in the batch scored fun 6.

edits.text: Mean legal actions per turn must exceed 5 and the share of forced (single-option) turns must stay under 0.05 at every player count.
edits.reason: mutiny (3.33 legal, depth 5), ransom (3.48, forced 0.163) and crossgrain (4.15, forced 0.208) were all called shallow or dense-but-slow by the judge; the games above 8 legal actions were not criticised on this axis.

edits.reason: Existing 0.05 rule was still breached: crossgrain 4p 0.312 vs 0.223, furlong 3p 0.377 vs 0.263, lamplighter 4p 0.30 vs 0.21, millwright 3p 0.283; judges attributed it to fixed lead/first-pick order in four games.

edits.text: Draw rate must stay under 0.05 at every player count; define a full deterministic tiebreak chain (score, then a secondary resource, then seat furthest from start) so ties cannot remain.
edits.reason: bindle reached a 0.203 draw rate at 4p (0.12 at 3p) and the judge marked it as games stalling into ties; every other game in the batch was near 0.

edits.text: Any hidden-role, hidden-VP, bluffing or simultaneous-selection design must make the hidden part decisive: hidden points >= 30% of a typical winning score, or the hidden role gets an action no other role has.
edits.reason: open-outcry's hidden vault was judged irrelevant because public portfolio+ticker dominate score; watchfire's saboteur had no unique action and its hidden-role tension was called thin; ransom's private peek had no way to be leveraged.

edits.reason: Clarity was 6 in 8 of 10 games; judges explicitly asked for a worked example in crossgrain, lamplighter and oubliette, and the two games with clarity 7 (open-outcry, bindle) were the ones with simpler scoring.
